userStories.title: Expose a unified quality contract on every workpack response
acceptance: AskResponse includes a qualityContract that combines fallback visibility, ontology QA readiness, evidence mapping coverage, structured document readiness, and DB persistence readiness.
The contract is built by a side-effect-free helper with focused unit tests.
Workspace UI renders the contract so the user can see whether the workpack is still template/fallback or ready for the integrated loop.

userStories.title: Wire ontology QA into the web workpack path, not only MCP
acceptance: Full/enhanced /api/ask workpacks run ontology QA against the selected task label.
The UI shows missing controls and review verdict as pre-submission checks.
Tests prove vague task labels are resolved consistently with the MCP path.

userStories.title: Refocus workspace into a 3-step workbench with improvement memory
acceptance: Workspace shows only the 3-step user flow: input, document, share.
The first screen is an extreme-simple white workbench with one question, one textarea, one primary action, and a thin evidence rail.
Document view focuses on risk assessment and TBM, with supporting documents collapsed behind +9 more.
Share view exposes scope, permissions, acknowledgement state, persistence ledger, and today's improvement candidates.
Before/After photos produce a reviewable improvement candidate with focused unit coverage.

userStories.title: Add DB consistency gates for workpack persistence
acceptance: Workpack save paths record qualityContract, ontologyQa, evidenceLabels, and structured metadata inside existing JSONB columns.
Reopen paths restore qualityContract, ontologyQa, evidenceLabels, and structured metadata without schema changes.
MCP token context rejects site/org attribution mismatch before inserting a workpack.
Evaluation report documents DB readiness without mutating existing production data.

userStories.title: Separate workspace into page-state navigation
acceptance: Workspace first load renders only the input page and does not render document, share, or empty-workspace sections below it.
Clicking generation moves the user into the document page where loading, evidence matching, and document preview live.
The 3-step rail acts as page-state navigation, not anchor scrolling; document/share are locked before a workpack exists.
Browser verification confirms desktop and mobile first load have no horizontal overflow and no first-screen document/share DOM.
Mobile evidence readiness rail does not require page-level horizontal scroll.

userStories.title: Replace fallback-first demo defaults with explicit live-readiness UX
acceptance: Template/mock modes are clearly labeled as demo paths, while full mode shows live-readiness blockers.
No screen implies legal completion when API or ontology evidence is missing.
Browser verification confirms the quality panel is visible and non-overlapping on desktop and mobile.
